generated_note: Injected deterministic timestamp, not wall clock.

1_sprint_overview.goal: Make printer-class acquisition possible in a memory-bounded, reproducible way, recovering the class that P4.3.2 left BLOCKED by a host-memory OOM.
1_sprint_overview.workflow: INVESTIGATE OOM -> BUILD LOW-MEMORY ADAPTER -> TEST -> DRY-RUN -> BOUNDED REAL ACQUISITION (limit 20 then 100) -> CONVERT/VALIDATE/QA -> REGRESSION -> STOP.
1_sprint_overview.outcome: Printer recovered to QA_PENDING with full evidence; no OOM; no other class touched; Dataset v1.0 NOT released.

did: Added one project-owned, thin low-memory acquisition adapter (scripts/acquire_openimages_lowmem.py) that plugs into the frozen P4.3.1 orchestrator through its existing DownloadFn seam.
Reused the frozen orchestrator, converter, validators, DuplicateDetector, provenance mechanism, visual-QA generator and report conventions verbatim.
Acquired only the printer class into its isolated per-class staging dir.
did_not: No YOLO training, no Dataset v1.0 release, no QA_ACCEPTED, no unrelated classes.

Did not merely raise the download limit, disable validation, delete annotations, fabricate labels, reduce QA requirements, change taxonomy, change image-quality thresholds, change provenance requirements, edit the vendored OIDv4_ToolKit, or fall back to another dataset.
No frozen intelligence/device_ai module (.py) was modified.

3_root_cause.summary: The vendored OIDv4_ToolKit loads the entire Open Images train bbox CSV in a single pandas.read_csv, inferring every column as object dtype; the frame balloons past host memory and the process dies before any image is fetched.
3_root_cause.observed_error: numpy._core._exceptions._ArrayMemoryError: Unable to allocate ... for an array with shape (14610229,) and data type object
3_root_cause.classification: Genuine host-memory constraint, not a mapping or data-absence problem (Printer -> printer is MAPPED; tablet/monitor read the same CSV successfully in P4.3.2).

4_remediation_design.approach: A thin, project-owned adapter that replaces only the fragile annotation-scan step with a memory-bounded chunked reader, then reuses the toolkit's own aws s3 --no-sign-request object layout and writes the exact OIDv4 per-class source layout the frozen converter already consumes.
4_remediation_design.integration_seam: acquire_openimages_multiclass.DownloadFn (DownloadRequest -> DownloadResult); orchestrator run(args, download_fn=...) injection. No new dataset architecture, no second annotation format.
4_remediation_design.chunked_read: pandas.read_csv(usecols=<11 of 13 columns>, dtype=<string/float32/int8>, chunksize=500000); each chunk filtered to the class MID (and any active attribute filters) before retention.
4_remediation_design.early_exit: Selection stops the instant a new distinct ImageID appears once --limit distinct ids are held; the bbox CSV is ImageID-contiguous, so every selected image is complete at that point.
4_remediation_design.determinism: First-seen CSV order until --limit distinct ids are held; identical CSV + limit selects an identical, fully-boxed set regardless of chunk size (verified by a chunk-size-parametrized test over [1,2,3,7,1000]).
4_remediation_design.source_fidelity: Exact source ImageIDs and exact source XYXY boxes preserved; normalized OID coords multiplied by the real downloaded image's pixel dimensions (same math as the vendored get_label).

7_source_class_mapping.resolved_from: dataset_acquisition/manifests/p4_3_1_openimages_acquisition_plan.csv (P4.3.1 plan manifest); MID resolved at runtime from class-descriptions-boxable.csv.

8_memory_evidence.note: Measured on this host with tracemalloc (Python peak) and Windows GetProcessMemoryInfo PeakWorkingSetSize (whole-process high-water mark) around a real scan of the full 1.19 GB CSV. Full detail in p4_3_3_memory_evidence.json.
8_memory_evidence.interpretation: Resident set stays a small fraction of the 1.11 GiB file because only leading chunks are streamed and columns are narrowed; the P4.3.2 OOM did not occur.

9_acquisition_target_and_ceiling_policy.ceiling_policy: Limit is a ceiling, not a promise. Actual availability recorded; never padded.

pilot_limit_20.note: Proved the full pipeline end-to-end with no OOM (20/20/20 reconciling) before scaling.

controlled_limit_100.gap_explained: 100 distinct ImageIDs were selected by the bounded scan; 96 landed as readable files from the public S3 bucket. 4 were unavailable/unreadable and are honestly reported as not downloaded (not padded).
